name: autopsy and cause of death overview
title: After a death: any coroner indication makes it a medicolegal case under the Coroner's Act; an expected natural death is certified by the doctor, who writes the cause of death in the WHO format, and a hospital autopsy needs informed authorization from the estate trustee or next of kin in order; a last row runs the steps of an autopsy across both kinds of autopsy and says what the death certificate is for

root.title: A patient has died: does the coroner need to know?
lines: call the coroner if ANY: family concerned about care · sudden and unexpected (no potentially fatal illness) · unnatural (accident, suicide, homicide) · death on a psychiatry ward · maternal death · seizure disorder · Children's Aid involved in a child's death
autopsy (necropsy, postmortem): same procedure either way, different focus · always by a pathologist

groups.title: YES: coroner's case
lines: sudden and unexpected, or any indication above

who: Part I: the causal chain, backwards

~hemopericardium ← ruptured myocardial infarct ← coronary atherosclerosis + thrombosis · II: diabetes
~upper GI bleed ← ruptured esophageal varix ← alcoholic cirrhosis · II: hemophilia
~right lung squamous cell carcinoma · II: tobacco smoking
Part II: contributed, outside the chain
often risk factors, e.g. diabetes, tobacco smoking
